scope: Finite-difference methods for linear elliptic/parabolic/hyperbolic PDEs; finite-volume methods for nonlinear scalar conservation laws; discrete consistency, stability, convergence, entropy, CFL, fluxes, splitting, energy and boundary treatment.

coverage.claim_contract: A theorem compares a specified continuum function with a grid or cell state through an explicit sampling/cell-average map and reconstruction, on a specified mesh family.
spaces_and_definitions: Grid states X_h and cell states U_K are mesh-dependent finite-dimensional spaces.
Uniform-grid norms include ||V||_(p,h)=(h sum_j |V_j|^p)^(1/p) and max norm; nonuniform grids need weights from cell/dual-cell measures.
Cell-average projection and point sampling are different maps and require different regularity assumptions.
Boundary nodes, ghost cells, periodic identification and incoming boundary data are part of the discrete state/operator definition.
source_evidence: MIT OCW lectures 5–6 and 19, full selected notes
Waterloo AM452, Chapter 2 PDF pp. 33–80 and Chapter 3 pp. 81–106
coverage.proof_completeness: The sources define model grids and norms and work examples. A general library interface must still choose conventions and make boundary closure explicit.

coverage.claim_contract: For a smooth exact solution u, the mesh residual tau_h=L_h I_hu-I_hLu (or the corresponding one-step scheme residual) is bounded in a named norm at a declared order; boundary residuals are included or separately bounded.
hypotheses: Enough derivatives of u for the Taylor expansion
An explicit boundary closure and its own order
A norm and asymptotic relation between dt and h for fully discrete schemes
proof_route: Insert sampled exact solution into the discrete operator.
Taylor-expand each stencil term with remainder under the stated regularity.
Treat interior and boundary rows separately.
For rough weak solutions, replace pointwise Taylor expansion with a weak/integral consistency argument rather than presuming smoothness.
source_evidence: MIT OCW lectures 5–6 and 15, full selected notes
coverage.proof_completeness: Oxford provides model proofs and order statements. Its nonlinear section only treats a smooth solution. The note cites Bramble–Hilbert for one rough-data estimate rather than proving that lemma.
missing_local_items: order theorem for a named stencil
weak consistency interface for nonsmooth solutions
non_inferences: Pointwise smooth consistency alone does not imply convergence at shocks or for rough weak solutions.

coverage.claim_contract: Stability is an h-uniform finite-time bound on the discrete solution operator in the comparison norm, including initial, forcing and boundary perturbations as relevant.
proof_route: Write the error recursion after subtracting the sampled exact solution.
Use the mesh-uniform propagator/operator bound on initial error and each residual contribution.
Sum the truncation errors over the time interval (or apply a discrete Gronwall estimate).
For stationary elliptic schemes, bound A_h^{-1} in the comparison norm and include the boundary residual.
source_evidence: Oxford 2025, §3 abstract linear boundary difference result and §§4–6 model schemes
MIT OCW lectures 6 and 14–15, complete selected notes
coverage.proof_completeness: Oxford has the model proof route; Waterloo provides matrix-power estimates for two-level schemes. A theorem must state the norm, time interval and boundary forcing contract.
non_inferences: A single-step spectral-radius test is not a uniform matrix-power bound, especially for non-normal or boundary-affected operators.

coverage.claim_contract: In Trefethen's abstract contract, B is a Banach space; u_t=Au is a well-posed linear IVP on 0<=t<=T for every u0 in B; each k fixes h=h(k) and a bounded linear S_k:B->B. Order-p>0 consistency is ||u(t+k)-S_k u(t)||=O(k^(p+1)) on sufficiently smooth exact solutions; convergence is S_k^n u0 -> u(t) for every u0 in B as k->0 and nk->t; stability is ||S_k^n||<=C_T uniformly for 0<=nk<=T. The same norm is used throughout. For a consistent approximation, convergence iff stability.
proof_route: For stability=>convergence, use e_n=sum_{j<n} S_k^(n-1-j)(S_k u(t_j)-u(t_{j+1})); uniform stability and O(k^(p+1)) local residual give O(k^p) error on a fixed interval for smooth data, then use density plus continuum continuous dependence for all data.

For convergence=>stability in the common-Banach-space setting, convergence for every u0 makes {S_k^n:0<=nk<=T} pointwise bounded because each continuum orbit is bounded on [0,T]; the Banach-space uniform boundedness principle then gives a uniform operator-norm bound.
source_evidence: Trefethen, full Chapter 4, PDF pp. 1–40 (printed pp. 147–185), especially §4.2/Theorem 4.1
Oxford 2025 §3, Theorem 6, is an elliptic residual theorem only and is not this IVP equivalence theorem
coverage.proof_completeness: Trefethen provides the exact theorem contract but explicitly marks its proof 'Not yet written' and identifies omitted rigor: the dense domain of A and the continuous/discrete norm relationship. The local published uniform boundedness principle supplies the converse proof step in the common-Banach formulation; the error recursion supplies the forward route. A grid-specific common embedding/norm equivalence remains an authoring obligation. MIT and Waterloo state the slogan/theorem but do not prove both directions.
missing_local_items: common Banach space or mesh embedding/reconstruction interface
well-posed linear IVP and dense smooth core contract
Lax–Richtmyer equivalence theorem with same-norm hypotheses and proof route
non_inferences: Do not apply this equivalence theorem to nonlinear finite-volume schemes.
Do not rename a direct elliptic residual estimate as Lax–Richtmyer equivalence.

coverage.topic: Elliptic finite differences and discrete energy/maximum principles
coverage.claim_contract: A specified elliptic stencil and boundary closure have a consistency estimate and a mesh-uniform inverse bound (or discrete maximum principle); the error equation then gives convergence in the corresponding norm.
proof_route: Define the grid inner product and discrete gradient.
Prove summation by parts with all boundary terms.
Use discrete Poincare/coercivity for energy stability, or sign/diagonal-dominance assumptions for a maximum principle.
Apply the residual error equation; use a different weak/integral route if solution regularity is too low for pointwise truncation.
source_evidence: MIT OCW lectures 5–6, full selected notes
coverage.proof_completeness: Oxford gives a full 1D proof, a 2D five-point energy proof and a discrete maximum-principle route, including rough-data caveats. Coefficient structure and boundary rows are scheme-specific.
non_inferences: Continuum Lax–Milgram does not prove discrete coercivity without a separate discrete form calculation.
Interior stencil order does not determine global order when boundary closure or solution regularity is limiting.

coverage.claim_contract: Fourier stability bounds the amplification symbol for constant-coefficient schemes on periodic/infinite uniform grids; CFL conditions are derived from characteristic/domain-of-dependence or scheme-specific monotonicity/energy calculations.
source_evidence: MIT OCW lectures 14–16, full selected notes
examples: Heat FTCS: kappa*dt/h^2 <= 1/2 in one dimension; multidimensional standard form dt*sum_i(kappa_i/h_i^2) <= 1/2
Centered explicit wave: c*dt/h <= 1 in one dimension
Scalar advection upwind monotonicity: 0 <= a*dt/h <= 1 for positive speed a
coverage.proof_completeness: The notes work these examples. Sufficient conditions vary with the actual stencil, dimension, geometry and boundary treatment.
missing_local_items: von Neumann amplification symbol and theorem scope
energy or matrix stability theorem for non-periodic/non-normal settings
non_inferences: A CFL inequality by itself is not a universal sufficient stability or convergence theorem.
Fourier-mode bounds do not automatically cover boundaries, variable coefficients or non-normal propagators.

coverage.topic: Parabolic theta schemes and discrete maximum principles
coverage.claim_contract: For the heat equation on the stated grid and boundary setup, consistency orders and L2 stability are proved separately from positivity/max-principle bounds.
source_evidence: MIT OCW lectures 4 and 14, complete selected notes
coverage.proof_completeness: Oxford derives the standard theta-scheme local orders, Fourier stability and stricter maximum-principle condition.
non_inferences: Unconditional L2 stability for theta >= 1/2 does not imply a discrete maximum principle; Crank–Nicolson can retain weakly damped high-frequency modes.

coverage.claim_contract: The scheme's discrete energy/flux identity includes boundary contributions; boundary data are prescribed for incoming characteristics, and the scheme-specific CFL/energy estimate controls the solution on the chosen interval.
coverage.proof_completeness: Oxford treats scalar hyperbolic IBVPs and inflow data; MIT lecture 18 contrasts inflow and outflow. System examples do not give a general nonlinear-system theorem.
missing_local_items: discrete integration by parts with boundary flux
non_inferences: Continuous energy conservation does not establish discrete conservation/stability.
An outflow boundary should not receive arbitrary prescribed data in the standard hyperbolic formulation.

coverage.topic: Conservative finite-volume update and numerical fluxes
coverage.claim_contract: Cell-average states evolve by shared interface flux differences; consistency F(u,u)=f(u) and flux cancellation give local conservation. This alone yields neither entropy admissibility nor convergence.
coverage.proof_completeness: Droniou and ETH supply scalar monotone-scheme proof material. Waterloo and MIT supply overview and flux construction only; Waterloo's printed formulas have errors and its limit theorem is not proof-bearing.
non_inferences: Conservation/RH compatibility does not select an entropy solution.

coverage.topic: Monotone scalar FV schemes and discrete entropy
coverage.claim_contract: A scalar consistent conservative flux monotone in its two arguments, together with a scheme-specific CFL bound, defines a monotone update with invariant range and a discrete Kruzhkov entropy inequality.
source_evidence: Droniou, full note pp. 1–39, especially monotone-scheme and convergence sections
MIT OCW lectures 17 and 19, complete notes for motivation
proof_route: Prove the update map is nondecreasing in all cell arguments under the CFL bound.
Use order preservation for the L-infinity interval bound and TVD for BV initial states.
Construct and verify the numerical entropy flux Q_k(a,b)=F(a vee k,b vee k)-F(a wedge k,b wedge k).
Derive the fully discrete entropy inequality from monotonicity and consistency.
coverage.proof_completeness: ETH supplies the monotone scalar convergence theorem and discrete entropy argument. The exact source theorem also assumes dt/dx >= c > 0 and BV data. Droniou cross-checks the BV route; its no-BV variant is only a sketch.
non_inferences: Linear Fourier stability is not nonlinear monotonicity or entropy stability.
An entropy inequality for the continuum equation cannot be inferred from conservation alone.

coverage.topic: Scalar FV convergence to entropy solutions
coverage.claim_contract: Under exact BV/CFL/flux hypotheses, a compactness argument yields a strongly convergent subsequence; consistency and conservation pass the weak equation, the discrete entropy inequality passes entropy admissibility, and uniqueness identifies the whole sequence.
source_evidence: ETH, Theorem 4.19 and Chapter 4 proof, PDF pp. 37–58
Droniou, full note pp. 1–39; BV proof and no-BV route distinction
proof_route: Uniform L-infinity and TV bounds plus time-translation estimate.
Helly/BV compactness in the scalar one-dimensional setting, or a separately proved Frechet–Kolmogorov argument with uniform tails/translations.
Conservative flux consistency passes the weak equation; the discrete entropy inequality passes to the entropy inequality.
Invoke Kruzhkov uniqueness to identify all subsequential limits and conclude full-family convergence.
exact_source_hypotheses: consistent conservative monotone two-point numerical flux
dt/dx >= c > 0 along the approximation family
coverage.proof_completeness: The discrete proof is detailed, but ETH cites Helly/BV compactness and imports entropy uniqueness; its appendix proves Gronwall only. Droniou's no-BV entropy-process route is not fully proved. A general arbitrary-L-infinity-data discrete convergence theorem is therefore not supplied by these notes.
missing_local_items: Helly selection/BV compactness (or an explicit alternate compactness proof)
discrete translation/time-modulus estimate if using Frechet–Kolmogorov
FV convergence theorem with exact interpolation/tail hypotheses
non_inferences: A uniform L-infinity bound alone does not give strong compactness.
The local published vanishing-viscosity compactness lemma is not the discrete FV compactness theorem.
Do not claim global L1 convergence on R without tail/integrability control.

coverage.claim_contract: A conservative, consistent scheme whose approximations converge with the required boundedness/integrability assumptions has a weak conservation-law solution as limit; entropy selection requires additional discrete entropy control.
source_evidence: Waterloo AM452, Chapter 3, PDF pp. 81–106 (the displayed statement is incomplete and unproved)
ETH/Droniou finite-volume entropy proofs for the special monotone scalar route
coverage.proof_completeness: The exact general theorem hypotheses and proof are not established by the sources read here. Treat this as a specific source/proof gap, not as a usable theorem statement.
missing_local_items: complete Lax–Wendroff theorem with boundedness/compactness or strong-convergence hypotheses
proof of weak limit passage by cell summation and flux consistency
non_inferences: The theorem does not imply entropy admissibility.

coverage.topic: High-order hyperbolic methods, TVD and SSP
coverage.claim_contract: High-order reconstruction is nonlinear near discontinuities; any claimed accuracy, invariant bounds or entropy property requires the hypotheses and proof for the limiter/reconstruction and time integrator together.
coverage.proof_completeness: Source coverage includes Godunov's linear monotonicity order barrier, TVD/SSP ideas and ENO/WENO constructions; it does not justify a blanket entropy-convergence theorem for every high-order method.
missing_local_items: TVD reconstruction and SSP convex-stability definitions
non_inferences: Formal smooth-region order does not ensure high-order behavior or convergence across a discontinuity.

coverage.claim_contract: For sufficiently regular flows of A and B, Lie splitting has first-order global accuracy and Strang splitting second-order global accuracy, with commutator and nested-commutator defects; stronger assumptions are required for unbounded PDE operators.
source_evidence: MIT OCW lecture 20, PDF pp. 1–3, complete note
proof_route: Expand one step of the split and unsplit flows.
Identify the commutator term for Lie and the nested commutators for Strang.
Accumulate local defect under a stability/regularity bound to obtain global order.
coverage.proof_completeness: The note proves/illustrates formal finite-dimensional or bounded-operator expansions; unbounded-operator domain and regularity claims remain obligations.
missing_local_items: global accumulation/stability argument and domain hypotheses
non_inferences: A formal commutator expansion is not by itself a rigorous PDE error bound.

coverage.claim_contract: A discrete energy estimate follows only after proving a grid summation-by-parts identity, handling boundary fluxes, and establishing positivity under the actual mesh/CFL constraints.
source_evidence: Oxford 2025, elliptic and wave sections, PDF pp. 26–53 and 76–110
Published local heat/wave continuum energy pages for model comparison
coverage.proof_completeness: The sources give model discrete energy arguments. No reusable local discrete summation-by-parts or boundary stability result exists.
non_inferences: The continuous energy identity does not imply a discrete one.

coverage.topic: Navier–Stokes formulation versus open regularity problem
coverage.claim_contract: The incompressible Navier–Stokes system and numerical projection schemes are established formulations/examples. The unresolved claim is specifically global smoothness and uniqueness for 3D classical solutions from smooth data; it is separate from stating or discretizing the equations.
coverage.proof_completeness: The lecture states the standard model and a projection-method example; it does not address global regularity.
missing_local_items: If desired, a separately sourced open-problem statement with exact 3D scope; never use it as a dependency for established formulation or numerical-method claims
non_inferences: Do not classify generic PDE/model formulation as an open problem.
Do not conflate local-in-time or 2D results, weak solutions, numerical convergence, and 3D global smoothness/uniqueness.

global_cautions: Lax–Richtmyer is linear IVP equivalence; Lax–Wendroff is a weak-limit theorem for conservative schemes. Keep them distinct.
Nonlinear convergence needs compactness and entropy selection; linear stability does not imply either.
Boundary closure and boundary forcing are part of consistency and stability.
BV/Helly compactness is not currently a local published supplier.
The scalar monotone convergence theorem does not imply a system convergence result.
Navier–Stokes equations are established models; the exact 3D regularity/uniqueness issue is a separate open claim, not a supplier.
